en.title: Can AI Help Gymnastics Judges Reduce Scoring Disputes?
en.intro: Xinhua Sports reports on a new AI judging support system and whether it can make gymnastics scoring less controversial.
paragraphs: Gymnastics moves happen in an instant. Small differences in body position or joint angle can affect move recognition and difficulty scores. At the recently concluded 54th World Gymnastics Championships, World Gymnastics Federation President Morinari Watanabe proposed introducing AI-assisted judging at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Whether this can reduce scoring disputes has become a topic of attention in the gymnastics community.

The system is called the Judging Support System (JSS). It was developed jointly by the World Gymnastics Federation and Fujitsu. Cameras capture video. AI identifies athletes' skeletal joint coordinates. Then, based on gymnastics scoring rules for movement structure and recognition criteria, the system analyzes the move. It provides judges with multi-angle replays and quantitative angle information.

JSS provides auxiliary information only. Official judgments are still made by human judges. The system has been used in cases where scores are withheld and during appeal reviews. It supports move recognition and difficulty assessment. The partnership began in 2017. JSS was first officially used at the 2019 Stuttgart World Championships in four events: rings, pommel horse, men's vault, and women's vault. At the 2023 Antwerp World Championships, it expanded to all 10 events.

At the 2025 Jakarta World Championships, JSS will be used by senior judging panels. Supervisors will also trial it in two events. At the Rotterdam World Championships, senior judges and supervisors across all 10 events used JSS officially. Difficulty judges also trialed it. Related data was used for athlete performance analysis. It was also used for arena big-screen displays and television broadcast explanations.

Chang Cheng, Director of the Gymnastics Management Center under China's General Administration of Sport, said AI assistance helps judges make more accurate judgments. But the system is 'not yet perfect'. It has produced some inaccurate results. He raised concerns about training adaptation. China's team does not yet have the same system. Teams face a new challenge: how to judge in daily training whether a move will be recognized by JSS. He also questioned the system's ability to distinguish subtle movement differences. Chang added that domestic research is underway to develop video-capture-based support systems. 'We also need to compete,' he said.

Fujitsu stated that JSS was further improved for the new cycle's scoring rules. Preliminary results show its accuracy at the Rotterdam competition reached the highest level so far. However, no specific accuracy rate or quantitative comparison with previous events was provided. Technology can add evidence for reviews. But whether it effectively reduces disputes requires more real-world application testing. Athletes and coaches must fully understand move recognition standards. They must receive corresponding feedback in training. These are key steps to building trust. Subject to relevant regulatory and export control requirements, JSS will be applied to all 10 events at the 2027 World Championships. Neither the World Gymnastics Federation nor Fujitsu confirmed whether it will be used at the Los Angeles Olympics. AI-assisted judging still needs practical refinement. Reducing scoring disputes requires not only more precise technology. It also requires clear rules and transparent procedures.

title: 蜘蛛怎样把蛋白浆纺成自然界最坚韧的丝
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 科学家首次在原子尺度看清，蜘蛛丝在变成固体纤维前，先经历一个液滴状的中间阶段——分子凝聚体。
paragraphs: 一只蜘蛛被人从墙上碰落，不会掉太久。就在几毫秒里，它把一包汤一样的蛋白质纺成一根结实的绳子，顺着这缕发亮的细丝爬回原处。这丝比防弹背心里那种叫凯夫拉的合成纤维更韧，强度也超过钢，还能弯曲，与人体相容。科学家一直想拿它做安全带、头盔、舰船材料，甚至做成帮助修复脑细胞的支架。可实验室里怎么都造不出同样好的蜘蛛丝，因为大家并不真正清楚，蜘蛛是怎样把丝腺里那包‘丝浆’纺成一根丝的。

丝浆不是现成的丝，而是蛋白质、水和盐混在一起的液体。一只蜘蛛能纺出多达七种丝：有的用来把猎物裹起来，有的做成有弹性的螺旋线吸收冲击，还有的当牵引丝，把网和蜘蛛固定在墙上。这些丝都由一类长条状的蛋白质构成，叫蛛丝蛋白，和胶原蛋白、角蛋白属于同一族。早在1907年，科学家就知道蜘蛛丝是蛋白质做的；又过了半个多世纪，X射线让人看到它的内部：排列整齐的蛋白薄片（称为β片层），嵌在一团不那么有序的非晶质基质里。
奇怪的地方在溶液里。把蛛丝蛋白溶开再看，它们并没有大多数蛋白质那样固定的形状，一大段一大段地飘来飘去，聚成形状又散开。这么一团乱糟糟的东西，怎么变成那么结实的纤维？早先有两种猜测：一种说这些蛋白质会像液晶那样彼此对齐，同时还能活动；另一种说它像蚕丝，先聚成一个个小圆球（即胶束），再压成丝。

要理解这团乱，得先绕到生物学的另一个地方去。2009年，科学家在受精的线虫卵里发现了一些浓缩着RNA的小液滴，后来这类东西被叫做‘凝聚体’。它是液体或者胶状的小泡，把分子攒在一起，却不把分子像固体那样锁死。因为它是流动的，生物可以把它捏成想要的形状。此后人们发现，活细胞里到处在用凝聚体：组织DNA、调控基因表达、打包蛋白质。在更大的尺度上，鱿鱼的喙靠它做出从硬到软的过渡，贻贝靠它牢牢粘在岩石上，沙堡虫靠它造出保护自己的管子。

2020年，京都大学的沼田圭司提出，蜘蛛丝从液体变成固体的过程中，也要经过凝聚体这一步，丝腺中部的磷酸盐可能启动了分子之间的相互作用。但原子层面到底怎么发生，还没有人讲清楚。圣地亚哥州立大学的化学家格雷戈里·霍兰带队去看了。研究生汉娜·约翰逊每隔几个月就收到一包雌性黑寡妇蜘蛛。黑寡妇有毒，但它们的牵引丝蛋白被研究得最透，而且全年都拿得到。他们用二氧化碳把蜘蛛麻醉，用镊子从蜘蛛腹部末端的纺器（即丝腺出口的细小孔道）上轻轻拉出丝，绕到由马达带动的小瓶上收起来；同时喂蜘蛛混了特定同位素的氨基酸，等于给蛋白质做上记号，好让仪器认出来。

约翰逊用核磁共振去看液体丝浆，以及从丝腺壶腹里取出的凝聚体；另一位研究者凯文·查莱克则测固体纤维里蛋白质的原子结构。他们想把两幅图对上：蛋白质在蜘蛛体内和在蜘蛛体外，明明是同一个东西，为什么表现如此不同。这项研究给出的答案是，丝浆里的分子先重组成半液体的凝聚体，再变成固体的丝纤维。霍兰说，搞清楚这套机制，是这个领域真正的‘圣杯’。麦吉尔大学的马修·哈林顿指出，凝聚体是许多生物反复使用的通用策略——看懂它，人们才有希望造出自然界最结实的那些材料。

en.title: How Spiders Turn Liquid Silk Into Tough Fiber
en.intro: Scientists are learning how a liquid mix inside a spider becomes one of nature's toughest fibers.
paragraphs: When a spider is knocked off a wall, it spins a soup of proteins into sturdy climbing gear within milliseconds. It uses a thin, shimmering strand of silk to haul itself back up. That strand is tougher than Kevlar. It is stronger than steel. It is flexible. It is biocompatible with human bodies. Scientists dream of making spider silk into seat belts, helmets, naval materials, and scaffolds to help repair brain cells. But lab attempts have fallen short. Researchers don’t know enough about how spiders spin 'silk dope'. Silk dope is a liquid blend of proteins, water, and salt. It comes from the spider’s silk glands. It turns into solid silk fiber.

Gregory Holland is a chemist and spectroscopist at San Diego State University. He called mapping the molecular mechanisms behind this process 'really the holy grail' for the field. He led research that described how molecules in liquid spider dope reorganize into semiliquid droplets. These droplets are called condensates. They form before turning into solid silk fiber. The result is an atomic-level look into the spider’s silk factory.

Condensates are used repeatedly by nature. They organize molecules for genetic processes. They help create impressively strong biological materials. Matthew Harrington is a biological materials scientist at McGill University. He was not involved in the study. He said it’s becoming clear that condensates are a common strategy across different organisms. Because they’re fluid, they’re malleable. Biology can shape them into whatever it wants.

Spiders are incredible natural factories. They can spin up to seven types of silks. Dragline silk anchors webs and spiders to walls. Spider silk is made of long, modular proteins. These proteins are called spidroins. The silk fiber contains flat sheets of protein. These sheets are known as beta sheets. They are embedded in a less ordered, non-crystalline matrix.

For decades, scientists wondered how a soup of unstructured proteins could organize into strong, solid fibers. Early theories included alignment in a dynamic 'liquid crystal' state. Another theory compared it to silkworm silk, where proteins organize into micelles. In 2020, Keiji Numata suggested spider silk undergoes a condensate phase. This happens during its transition from liquid dope to solid thread. Condensates form by 'liquid-liquid phase separation'. In this process, molecules in a liquid start to interact weakly. They form bonds easily. They break bonds easily. This can be triggered by a change in pH, chemicals, or temperature. Numata proposed phosphate in the ampulla might initiate these interactions. The ampulla is the middle section of a spider’s silk gland.

Hannah Johnson was a graduate student in Holland’s lab. She studied black widow spiders. Every few months in 2023 and 2024, packages of female black widows arrived at San Diego State University. The spiders were knocked unconscious by carbon dioxide. Johnson and several students 'silked' the spiders. They used tweezers to gently pull silk from the spinnerets. They wound the silk around a vial with a spinning motor. The team fed the spiders amino acids enriched with particular isotopes. Johnson called them 'protein shakes'. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy can map the structure of a molecule. Johnson used NMR on liquid spider dope. She also used it on condensates collected from the spiders’ ampullae. Kevin Chalek was a postdoctoral researcher in Holland’s lab. He mapped the atomic structure of the proteins in the solid fiber. They aimed to bridge the gap between what happens when the protein is inside the spider and when it’s outside.

title: 他亲身遭遇雪崩，后来成了雪崩预报员
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 一场把自己埋住的雪崩，把一名环境科学学生推上了研究雪、预报雪崩的路。
paragraphs: 2017年5月19日，克里斯·迪克森在科罗拉多州西南部的圣胡安山脉滑雪。他特意去试最近几场暴风雪积下的新雪。可那层新雪并不稳定，他遇上了雪崩，被雪部分埋住。他用 crunching motion（挤压挣脱）的方式让自己脱身。他说：‘That was a very scary eye-opener to the potential hazard of avalanches.’ 当时他搬到科罗拉多是为了学环境科学，这场雪崩改变了他的目标。他说：‘[It] inspired me to want to help other people avoid having that experience.’
他先成为雪崩教育者，教人们冬天如何在山里安全行动。后来他更想弄懂雪崩背后的科学，想花更多时间挖雪、分析雪。现在，他在丹佛的科罗拉多雪崩信息中心做雪崩预报员，每天制作预报，帮助公众在出发前了解雪崩风险。他说：‘I’m incredibly lucky that I survived. I took that lesson as a real learning opportunity.’

他提到，很多人误以为这份工作主要靠实地经验，其实非常依赖电脑。电脑建模和技术帮他们预测无法徒步抵达区域的雪况，也是向公众传达危险的主要方式。他主要看气象站的风和降水读数，也读公众提交的观察记录。他说：‘I actually spend more time at the computer than I do in the mountains. I’d say I enjoy them both, but it’s much nicer to be in the mountains than at the computer.’

在野外工作的日子，他出发前先用电脑数据做一份计划，包括大量地图作业来规划路线，并与同事共享计划，由同事进行野外作业检查。他要说明当天想重点观测的目标、地点、同行者，以及如何管理风险。然后进山四到八小时收集数据。很多是肉眼观察：找最近雪崩的痕迹，看脚下的地形；也专门去朝向特定方向、处于特定海拔的坡面。他会挖雪坑观察雪层结构，也会做稳定性测试：隔离雪柱后敲击雪层施加应力。这些数据用于撰写预报，公众当晚就能看到，用来计划第二天的野外活动。

最难忘的经历，往往是调查已经发生的雪崩。只要事件涉及人，他们就会去查，尤其是有人受伤、被埋甚至死亡的时候。去年冬天，他的一位朋友在滑雪场外被一场很大的雪崩卷走，被带过悬崖，经历非常可怕，幸好活了下来。这让他特别想弄明白为什么会发生。人们常问自己是不是做错了什么。有时自然雪崩会困住人，他们可能根本不知道自己身处危险区；有时则是人走进了风险更高的地方。分析朋友那次雪崩后，他告诉朋友：‘you could’ve avoided triggering the avalanche by skiing about 30 feet [9 meters] to either side.’ 他说那是‘an unlucky situation of being in the wrong place at the wrong time’。这样的调查能给人交代，也总能让人学到东西。

如果给年轻的自己建议，他会说：‘do the work you want to be paid for eventually.’ 他发起播客项目‘San Juan Stormcast’，因为他感觉人们想要一种不同于传统渠道的信息形式。雪崩信息很严肃，通常讲得非常直接，播客让他能多一点趣味，也发展自己的表达方式。他决定把公共安全信息分享给尽可能多的人，当时没人付钱给他。但这份工作给了他后来得到现在职位的基础技能和曝光。他说：‘If you wish you had a resource that no one else has created, just go ahead and build it yourself.’

title: 女孩拿农场里的24种植物做实验，看它们能不能杀死细菌
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 美国俄克拉何马州的一位切罗基族女孩，把自家农场里的24种植物煮成提取液，测试它们的抗菌能力：没有一种强过现有药物，但其中13种确实杀死了一部分细菌。
paragraphs: 美国俄克拉何马州的一座农场里，14岁的洛克琳·沃德有个傍晚在帮家里喂牛。喂着喂着，她的目光落到了田里那些自生的植物上。她知道，科学家一直在寻找对付感染的新办法，于是冒出一个念头：长在我家农场的这些植物，能不能杀死细菌？
她挑了24种植物，其中12种是俄克拉何马州的本土植物。她把植物切成一克（约0.04盎司）的小块，再分别用水煮，把里面的化学物质提取出来。接着，她拿两种细菌做试验：大肠杆菌（_Escherichia coli_）和表皮葡萄球菌（_Staphylococcus epidermidis_）。她也测试了目前用来治疗感染的抗生素作为对照。
方法很直观：她把小纸片泡在植物提取液或抗生素中，再把纸片放到含细菌的培养皿里。如果提取液有抗菌作用，纸片周围的细菌就会死亡。结果是：没有一种农场植物的提取物比现有抗生素更有效。不过，24种植物中有13种确实杀灭了一部分细菌，其中包括7种本土植物。
这离‘新药’还很远，但洛克琳希望这个结果能指向新的思路。当前抗生素被过度使用，导致越来越多的细菌产生耐药性，因此急需新方案。

洛克琳是切罗基族公民。她说：‘Growing up, my grandmother often talked with me about how plants and herbs can be used for medicine and healing,’ ‘And as a citizen of the Cherokee Nation, I’ve always been interested in learning more about plants and their traditional and potential medicinal uses.’ 这个项目是她在俄克拉何马州格罗夫市格罗夫中学读八年级时完成的，后来让她入围了2026年Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge决赛。该挑战赛由科学学会（Society for Science）主办，该机构也出版《Science News Explores》。

被问到最大的困难是什么，洛克琳说：‘Managing my time, because I’m involved in many extracurriculars.’ 她提到教会活动和体育运动让日程很紧张，研究只能靠周末和放学后的零散时间，有时还得推掉其他有趣安排；她用谷歌日历管理时间，‘That helped a lot.’ 她最重要的资源是科学展指导老师：‘She’s the one if I got bad results, she’d be like, “It’s okay, Locklyn, just keep going.”’ 她给科学展新手的建议是：找一位像这样的导师，在困难和压力时期帮你保持动力。

en.title: A Teen Tests Farm Plants for Germ-Fighting Power
en.intro: Science News Explores reports that a fourteen-year-old in Oklahoma turned a farm chore into a science-fair project about plants and bacteria.
paragraphs: Locklyn Ward, 14, lives on a farm in Oklahoma. One evening while she was helping feed the cows, she got curious about the plants growing in the field. She knew that scientists are always searching for new ways to fight infections. So she set out to see if any of the plants growing on her family’s farm could take down bacteria.

Locklyn picked 24 plants; 12 were native to her state. She cut the plants into one-gram (four hundredths of an ounce) pieces and boiled each to extract chemicals from it. Then, she tested those extracts against two types of bacteria: _Escherichia coli_ and _Staphylococcus epidermidis_. Locklyn also tested antibiotics that are currently used to treat infections.

The test involved paper disks soaked in either the plant extracts or current antibiotics. Locklyn placed those soaked disks into dishes containing bacteria. If chemicals from the farm plants had antibiotic powers, the bacteria around those paper disks would die. No farm-plant extract worked as well as current medicines. But 13 of the 24 plants did kill some bacteria. These included seven native plants.

Locklyn hopes her results may point to new ways to fight germs. Overuse of current antibiotics is leading to more drug-resistant bacteria, so new solutions are much needed. Locklyn did this project as an eighth grader at Grove Middle School in Grove, Okla. Her research earned her a finalist spot in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.

Growing up, her grandmother often talked with her about how plants and herbs can be used for medicine and healing. And as a citizen of the Cherokee Nation, Locklyn has always been interested in learning more about plants and their traditional and potential medicinal uses. Managing her time was the biggest challenge, because she’s involved in many extracurriculars — including church activities and sports. She used Google Calendar to help. Her science-fair teacher encouraged her after bad results, saying, 'It’s okay, Locklyn, just keep going.' Locklyn’s biggest piece of advice for science fair newbies is to find a mentor like this to help stay motivated.

title: 一块人造玻璃标样，帮科学家读懂嫦娥六号月壤里的撞击者
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 中国科学院广州地球化学研究所的团队在实验室合成含铂族元素的玻璃标样PGE-BG1，用它对嫦娥六号月壤熔结玻璃开展原位微区分析，估算出其中约1.1–4.6 wt%的陨石物质，并推测撞击体主要为球粒陨石和IIAB铁陨石。
paragraphs: 月球上没有空气，也没有水，几十亿年来，无数小天体直接撞在月面上。撞击的一瞬间，岩石被熔化，又迅速冷却，结成熔结玻璃。这些玻璃里留着撞击者的化学痕迹。但痕迹极淡，而月壤每一克都极其珍贵。中国科学院广州地球化学研究所月球样品研究小组硕士研究生高佳俊在该所正高级工程师张乐指导下，根据嫦娥五号/六号熔结玻璃的主量元素组成配置初始物，采用高温马弗炉熔融法，在实验室合成含铂族元素（PGEs）的玻璃标样PGE-BG1。

他们关注的是铂族元素，包括钌（Ru）、铑（Rh）、钯（Pd）、锇（Os）、铱（Ir）、铂（Pt）和铼（Re）。这七种元素均属强亲铁元素，是示踪陨石物质、撞击事件和行星演化的重要‘地球化学指纹’。传统溶液法分析PGEs常需数百毫克至数克样品，难以满足月壤等珍贵地外样品的微区分析需求；LA-ICP-MS虽可实现几十微米尺度原位分析，却依赖基体匹配、组成均一的参考物质。现有NIST、USGS系列玻璃标样的PGEs含量约束不足，均匀性也有争议。

研究团队发现，使用铂金坩埚会使除铂外的PGEs强烈扩散进入坩埚而丢失；改用刚玉坩埚后避免了这一损失。初始物先在1000℃保温10小时去除二氧化碳，再在1500℃保温4小时后在去离子水中淬火。合成玻璃与坩埚接触界面存在约500微米成分扩散剖面，团队切除边部和底部，选取未受影响区域分析。电子探针显示，PGE-BG1主量元素2RSD小于3.3%；溶液ICP-MS定值与LA-ICP-MS微区结果在误差范围内一致，Rh、Pd、Ir、Pt、Re的2RSD小于15%。受高温挥发影响，Ru和Os几乎完全丢失，推测被氧化为RuO₄和OsO₄挥发；Re丢失超过90%，说明PGEs在高温熔融中存在明显元素间分馏。

以PGE-BG1为外标，团队测试了常用玻璃标样GSD-1G和NIST 610，并对嫦娥六号月壤熔结玻璃开展原位微区分析。结果显示，嫦娥六号熔结玻璃成分变化较大：FeO为8.8–26.2 wt%，Al₂O₃为8.1–20.4 wt%，Th从低于检出限至5.7 μg/g。多数测试点在FeO–Al₂O₃和FeO–Th关系图中位于高地斜长岩与月海玄武岩之间并靠近月海玄武岩端元，表明其主要物质来源为本地月海玄武岩，同时混入高地物质和少量KREEP组分。
熔结玻璃Ni含量为215–887 μg/g，显著高于本地月海玄武岩（约15 μg/g），且Ir与Ni明显正相关。质量平衡计算显示，其中含约1.1–4.6 wt%的陨石物质；Co–Ni关系指示撞击体可能主要为球粒陨石和IIAB铁陨石。样品未检测到Ru和Os信号，说明撞击形成熔结玻璃过程中PGEs发生了显著分馏，采用PGEs示踪撞击体类型时需考虑这一影响。
该研究合成的PGE-BG1硅酸盐玻璃标样，为嫦娥六号月壤熔结玻璃PGEs和Re的微区分析提供了可靠外标，也为识别撞击体性质、理解月表撞击与空间风化过程提供了新的分析支撑。相关成果发表于《分析原子光谱学杂志》，论文信息：https://doi.org/10.1039/d6ja00343e。

title: 全新岗位快速涌现 职业教育如何“跟得上”？
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 新技术带来一批以前没有的工作，学校教的内容要怎样追上岗位变化的速度？
paragraphs: 有些职业的名字，几年前还几乎没人提起，如今已经出现在身边。新岗位在快速涌现，这是中新网教育这篇文章标题里点出的变化。它同时留下了一个问题：职业教育，要怎么“跟得上”？
难点首先在时间上。一个专业从设立、招生，到学生学成走向岗位，通常要经过好几年；而外面的岗位还在继续变化。如果课程完全照着今天的需求来定，等学生毕业，面对的可能是另一批工作。
这又牵出一个更细的选择：哪些内容要教得具体，哪些要教得通用。具体到某一种工具、某一套流程，学的时候上手快，可工具一换就得重新学；而理解背后的道理、会动手排查问题、能和别人配合，这些本领换到别的岗位上也能继续用。
还有一层在学校之外：行业里正在发生什么变化，谁把消息带给学校，学校又怎样据此调整课程。这条通道顺不顺畅，决定了调整是早一步还是晚一步。新技术还会不断冒出新岗位，而一门课要陪一个学生走好几年，这个时间差恐怕没有一次就能解决的答案。

title: 未来的电路，也许不必长在平板电路板上
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 美国国家科学基金会支持的研究者伊桑·塞科尔介绍一种专门的增材制造技术、它所涉及的材料，以及由此做出、可以针对复杂三维表面定制的电路。
paragraphs: 我们身边的电子设备，几乎都建立在一块平板电路板上。手机、耳机、汽车仪表盘，拆开来看，核心往往是一片薄薄的、平的板子。可真实世界的表面很少是平的：手腕是圆的，机翼是弯的，很多东西的形状都不规整。于是问题来了——电路一定要长在平板上吗？
美国国家科学基金会（NSF）在2026年10月27日发布的一期播客里，讨论了这个问题。受访者是受NSF支持的研究者伊桑·塞科尔（Ethan Secor）。这期节目属于NSF的播客《NSF Discovery Files》，可以在各播客平台收听。
按NSF的介绍，塞科尔在节目里讲了三件事：一种专门的增材制造技术、这种技术涉及的材料，以及用它们做出来的电路——这些电路可以针对复杂的三维表面进行定制。
NSF的表述是，这些电路可以针对复杂的三维表面做定制。也就是说，被讨论的不只是一种新的制造手段，还有电路与承载它的形状之间的关系：当表面不再是平板，电路要如何跟着形状来安排。
NSF在页面开头写了一句很大的话：新的、有雄心的想法，是下一代技术的地基。这句话放在这里并不空。
如果想继续追下去，可以顺着两条线自己想：一是形状，为什么平面限制了设计；二是材料，一种材料要满足什么条件，才能既被“添加”上去，又能导电。

title: 动物血液不只有红色：章鱼血呈蓝色，南极冰鱼血几乎透明
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 从章鱼的蓝血到南极冰鱼近乎透明的血，动物界的血液颜色比我们想的丰富得多，而每一种颜色背后都对应一套运送氧气的办法。
paragraphs: 鼻子碰破了，手指扎破了，流出来的血总是红的。可要是把整个动物界看一遍，红色只是众多答案里的一个。有的动物血是蓝的，有的是紫的，有的是绿的，还有的是乳白色、几乎透明的。同样是运送氧气的液体，为什么颜色能差这么多？

先说我们自己。血液的红色来自血红蛋白，它是红细胞里的一种蛋白质，里面装着铁原子。铁原子抓住氧气，血就显得鲜红；氧气少了，颜色就变成发暗的褐红。章鱼、鱿鱼，还有虾和蟹，用的是一种叫血蓝蛋白的蛋白质，里面装的是铜原子。铜原子抓住氧气会发蓝，它们的血因此是蓝色的，鲎也就是马蹄蟹，同样是一身蓝血。血蓝蛋白抓氧的效率不如血红蛋白，但它在低温下工作得特别好，深海正合适。研究还提示，它可能不只负责运氧，比如参与免疫、帮助伤口愈合。
腕足动物和生活在海底的花生虫，血是紫色的，它们用的是一种含铁、本身发紫的蛋白质，叫血赤蛋白。海鞘这种软软的、像土豆一样的海洋动物，血是黄绿色的，原因目前还有争论：一种说法和它们血液里富集的钒有关，另一种说法和吃有关，它们消化海水里的浮游植物时会产生类胡萝卜素，这类色素是黄、红或者橙色的。
新几内亚有几种蜥蜴，运送氧气用的还是血红蛋白，但它们会把血红蛋白分解成一种天生的绿色色素，叫胆绿素。人得黄疸时皮肤呈现黄绿色，也是这个分子在高浓度下的效果。多数脊椎动物会继续把胆绿素分解成别的、颜色暗淡的物质，这几种蜥蜴不这么做，色素在血液里越积越多，最后绿色盖过了血红蛋白的红色。

南极冰鱼是目前已知唯一不制造血红蛋白、也没有红细胞的脊椎动物，血液是乳白半透明的，研究者形容它们像幽灵一样。它们不靠任何抓住氧气的蛋白质，而是让氧气直接溶进血液。它们的身体也做了配套改动：心脏和毛细血管比别的南极鱼更大，能泵出和循环更多的血；捕食时不追不跑，埋伏着等猎物靠近，耗能少，需要的氧也少。冰鱼的血红蛋白基因为什么会从DNA里消失？这仍是谜，研究者连先失去红细胞还是先失去血红蛋白都还说不清。一个猜想是：南大洋的水又冷又富含氧气，氧气足够直接进入血液，血红蛋白这个中间人就显得多余了。

海拔越高，氧气越稀薄，鹿鼠却能生活在海拔约四千多米的地方，比很多人开始出现高原反应的高度还高得多。它的血红蛋白和氧结合得特别紧，安第斯山的蜂鸟和高原上的黑斑蛙也有类似的改变。不过适应总有代价，结合得太紧，氧气就不容易松开、送进组织。鹿鼠的补偿办法是让肌肉纤维里多一些能释放氧的线粒体。研究这些奇怪的血，也可能帮到人：鹿鼠的血红蛋白演化或许能启发慢阻肺这类缺氧疾病的治疗；而对全球近二十亿贫血的人来说，那身透明血的南极冰鱼，也许藏着线索。

en.title: Why Animal Blood Comes in So Many Colors
en.intro: Blood is not always red. The colors reveal how different animals survive in their environments.
paragraphs: When you scrape your knee, the blood you see is red. But red is not the only color for blood in the animal kingdom. Some creatures bleed blue. Some bleed green or yellow. Antarctic blackfin icefish bleed ghostly white. Scientists have studied these colors to understand how blood works.

In humans and many animals, a protein called hemoglobin carries oxygen. Hemoglobin contains iron atoms. When iron binds oxygen, blood is bright cherry red. When less oxygen is bound, it’s a muddier brown-red. Octopuses, squid, shrimp, and crabs use hemocyanin instead. It contains copper atoms, which look blue when bound to oxygen.

Some marine creatures — like clam-like brachiopods and peanut worms — bleed violet. They use hemerythrin, an iron-rich purple protein. Some sea squirts bleed greenish yellow. One candidate for the color is vanadium. Another theory points to diet: metabolizing marine phytoplankton creates yellow-orange carotenoids. Several lizard species in New Guinea have green blood. They break down hemoglobin into biliverdin — a green pigment — and accumulate it so highly that it overwhelms the red of hemoglobin.

Antarctic blackfin icefish of the family Channichthyidae are the only known vertebrates that do not make hemoglobin and do not have red blood cells. Their blood is milky, translucent white. Instead of hemoglobin, oxygen dissolves directly into their bloodstream. They have larger hearts and capillaries, and they are patient ambush predators — lying in wait rather than darting, so they expend less energy and need less oxygen.

In high-altitude ecosystems, some species have evolved hemoglobin that binds oxygen more tightly. The deer mouse lives up to 14,000 feet above sea level. Its hemoglobin makes extra tight bonds with oxygen. But this makes it harder to release oxygen into tissues. To compensate, the mouse has higher quantities of oxygen-releasing mitochondria in its muscle fibers.

These unusual blood systems may inform human health. Deer mouse hemoglobin evolution could inspire therapies for hypoxia-inducing diseases, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Icefish — transparent bleeders — may hold clues for treating anemia. As Postlethwait says, 'the icefish have figured it out.'

title: 紧张时身体会自动加速，科学家正研究如何主动让它慢下来
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 压力来的时候，身体会自动加速；科学家正在弄清楚，我们怎样主动踩下那脚刹车。
paragraphs: 考试前，或者要上台前，你可能有过这样的体验：压力激素涌进血液，心跳变快，血压升高，呼吸也变急。这些反应都不经过思考，由交感神经系统自动启动。不管你面对的是真正的危险，还是一场大考，它都会出手。交感神经的另一套系统叫副交感神经系统，负责把身体带回休息状态：降低压力激素、放慢心跳、降低血压。纽约大学朗格尼医学中心的神经科医生帕特里西奥·米拉尔·韦尔内蒂说：‘ consciously, you can’t tell your heart to slow down.’ 但通过一些干预，你能多一点掌控。
其中一个关键角色是迷走神经。它从脑干延伸到腹部，呼吸练习可以激活它，冷水疗法也可能有同样作用。有一项小研究：科学家让25人做心算，其中12人此前戴过一种面部冷却面罩，用来模拟把脸浸入冷水中——这是已知的刺激迷走神经的方法。所有人都因心算而紧张，但戴过面罩的人释放的皮质醇更少，恢复得也更快。皮质醇是一种压力激素。这项研究发表在《Scientific Reports》上。
哼唱也进入了研究者的视线。2025年10月的一项研究显示，慢呼吸加上哼唱可以提升心率变异性——即心跳间隔时间的波动程度。高心率变异性是神经系统调节良好的标志之一，物理治疗师卡琳·斯蒂尔解释说，这表示‘你的身体内部正在减少自我对抗’，也更能灵活切换压力与放松状态。她在华盛顿州塔科马市的普吉特海湾大学工作。
还有一种做法是轻拍皮肤特定部位。研究显示，这种拍打可降低压力激素水平，也能减缓心率和降低血压。它甚至被用于某些状况的辅助治疗，比如创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。2025年的一篇综述提出，拍打可能向大脑发送信号，促使副交感神经系统接管。

那么哪一种方法最好？波士顿麻省总医院本森—亨利身心医学研究所的达尔尚·梅塔说：‘There’s really no one best way.’ 他指出，网上几乎每种流行技巧都能找到支持它的小型、一次性研究。真正重要的是找到适合自己的方法并坚持练习。他说：‘It’s not important which practice [people adopt]… What’s important… is that people do practice [it].’ 帕特里西奥·米拉尔·韦尔内蒂补充说，哼唱和吟诵等做法早已存在于古老的精神实践中，‘People have been doing [them] for centuries.’
这些方法不是魔法开关，而是给身体多一个调节选项。它们背后的研究大多规模较小，效果也因人而异。慢而深的呼吸，也许是你早就用过的那一个。那么下一次紧张来临，你愿意先试哪一个？

title: 铁三世界杯韩国统营站：中国选手包揽女子冠、亚军
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 在2026年10月24日举行的铁人三项世界杯韩国统营站比赛中，中国选手林鑫瑜和黄安琪包揽女子优秀组冠、亚军，总成绩分别为56分42秒和56分45秒。
paragraphs: 先记住两个数字：56分42秒，56分45秒。这是10月24日铁人三项世界杯韩国统营站女子优秀组的冠军和亚军成绩，拿到它们的，是两位中国选手——林鑫瑜和黄安琪。第三名是法国选手玛蒂尔德·戈蒂埃（从左至右：黄安琪、林鑫瑜、戈蒂埃）。一场国际比赛，领奖台上最高的两级同时站着中国选手，这是中国铁人三项的历史时刻。
铁人三项要先游泳，再骑自行车，最后跑步，三个项目连着完成，中间不停表。统营站这天，林鑫瑜和黄安琪在游泳和自行车赛段都待在第一集团中。在跑步赛段中，黄安琪最先建立起领跑优势，但在第一圈结束时因罚时10秒而落后；前方，林鑫瑜与葡萄牙选手玛丽安娜·瓦尔热姆展开激烈角逐。在一个上坡阶段，林鑫瑜发力实现超越，一路领先至终点。
凭借出众的跑步能力，黄安琪在后方持续追击，反超多名选手，最终以总成绩56分45秒收获亚军，刷新个人在此项赛事中的最好成绩。虽然比赛过程曲折，但她始终保持了平稳的心态。她在赛后说：“能和队友一起站上领奖台我非常开心，这是中国铁三的历史时刻。下一步我们依然会打好每一场积分赛，全力冲击奥运资格。”
林鑫瑜赛后表示：“（我）延续了北京世界杯时的身体状态和感觉，做好了赛中决策，把整个周期的训练成果都在比赛中发挥出来了。”上一站世界杯为中国队首夺该系列赛事金牌后，林鑫瑜在统营站以总成绩56分42秒蝉联冠军。

title: 银鳕鱼被下架后，要厘清的是鱼被误读还是吃鱼规则
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 一位母亲的网上发帖，让银鳕鱼从高档辅食变成了被下架的商品，也让“汞”这个字进了很多家庭的餐桌对话。
paragraphs: 9月27日，杭州一位母親在網上發帖：過去8個月，她每週給2歲的孩子吃兩到三次從盒馬買的「兒童裝」銀鱈魚，本是看重商家宣傳的銀鱈魚營養好，孩子多吃魚更健康，結果卻導致孩子血汞超標，需要做排汞治療。
帖子發出後，家長們紛紛翻出自己的購物訂單，擔心孩子也被「投毒」。盒馬在內的多個平臺下架了銀鱈魚，或者刪去商品頁上的「兒童」、「寶寶」字樣。據澎湃新聞報道，十一假期前後，上海新華醫院的「環境污染物中毒」門診出現就診高峰，家長們紛紛帶着1至3歲的孩子來查血汞，門診還臨時加開了一天，不少孩子——他們大多沒有任何症狀，在醫生的建議下接受藥物排汞。
10月5日，國家食品安全風險評估中心發布《關於人群食用深海魚類的消費提示》，提醒孕哺期婦女和嬰幼兒儘量避免汞含量高的魚種，並把銀鱈魚列入甲基汞含量通常較高的大型肉食性魚類。一週之內，一條魚從高檔輔食變成了「投毒」嫌疑犯。
但這場爭議裏有太多概念被混淆：「銀鱈」和「鱈魚」是什麼關係？汞超標到底有多嚴重？低汞魚是不是就可以放開吃？釐清這些，才能看清風波真正暴露的問題。
撰稿人把這場風波裡被混淆的概念，歸成了三個問題。第一，「銀鱈」和「鱈魚」到底是什么關係，名字裡都帶鱈，是不是同一種魚？第二，汞超標到底有多嚴重，超到什麼程度、吃多久才算危險？第三，低汞的魚是不是就可以放開吃？文章說，只有把這三個問題釐清，才能看清風波真正暴露出來的東西。
這場風波里，我們真正缺少的是一套讓所有人都用得上的規則。一條魚能不能吃，背後其實是一整套規則：哪種魚適合哪個年齡的人吃，吃多少，多久吃一次；包裝上寫下「兒童」兩個字時，依據的是什麼；出了問題，家長去哪裡查、找誰問。餐桌上的「銀鱈魚」也許會回來，但如果缺一套拿起來就能用的規則，下次換一個魚的名字，同樣的慌亂還會再來一遍。

en.title: The Silver Cod Scare: Was It the Fish or the Rules?
en.intro: When one mother's online post about her toddler and a fish called silver cod spread, parents across China started checking their freezers and rushing to hospitals.
paragraphs: In about one week, a fish went from a fancy food for babies to a suspect. In late September, a mother in Hangzhou wrote a post online about her two-year-old child. For eight months, she had given the child silver cod two or three times a week. She bought it from a Chinese grocery chain called Hema, sold in a package meant for children. She chose it because the marketing said silver cod was nutritious, and that children who eat more fish are healthier. Then came the result she did not expect. Her child's blood mercury was above the standard, and the child needed treatment to clear it.

Other parents read the post and began searching their own order histories. Many feared their children had been harmed too. Hema and other platforms took silver cod off their shelves. Some simply deleted the words 'children' and 'baby' from the product pages. According to reporting by The Paper, around the National Day holiday, Shanghai Xinhua Hospital's clinic for poisoning by environmental pollutants had a rush of visits. Parents brought children between one and three years old to have their blood mercury checked. The clinic even opened one extra day. Many of those children had no symptoms at all, and still received medicine to remove mercury on doctors' advice.

Then, on October 5, the National Center for Food Safety Risk Assessment published a consumer notice about eating deep-sea fish. It advised pregnant and breastfeeding women, and infants and young children, to avoid fish that carry high levels of mercury. The notice named silver cod among large predatory fish that usually contain more methylmercury. But the article points out how much got mixed together in the argument. People were not sure what the real link is between silver cod and ordinary cod. They were not sure how serious it is when blood mercury goes above the line. And they were not sure whether low-mercury fish can simply be eaten without limits.

The author, a genetics PhD and science writer, argues that clearing up these confusions is the only way to see what the scare really exposed. A mother shared a real experience. A warning was issued about which fish some people should avoid. Between those two things, a lot of questions are still open. A fish did not suddenly change. Our understanding of it did.

Maybe the real question is not which fish to fear. Maybe it is whether families have clear rules they can actually use. Rules about how often to eat which fish, and who should be extra careful. Without those rules, every worried post turns into a shopping panic. With them, parents could make a calm choice at the counter. And children could keep eating fish, without anyone needing to be scared of dinner.

title: 甘肃肃北牧区立法守护千年岩画
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 甘肃肃北的牧区决定用一部法律，把散落在旷野里的千年岩画纳入保护。
paragraphs: 在甘肃肃北的牧区，有一些图画比文字还要老。它们不是画在纸上，而是留在旷野的岩石上，一留就是上千年。最近，当地决定用一部法律来守护它们。
先说背景。岩画，就是古人在岩石上凿刻或者画下的图像。它和博物馆里的文物有个最大的不同：它通常留在自己被创作出来的那个地方，山坡上、河谷边、牧场的石壁上。它没法被搬进恒温恒湿的展柜，只能和风、雨、日光，还有一代代从这里经过的人待在一起。
那“立法守护”是什么意思？法律和一句口号的区别，在于它把话写下来，并且公开：什么可以做，什么不可以做，出了事该找谁。它不依赖某个人的记性，也不依赖某一届人一时的重视——换一批人来做，条文还在。对一件还要在原地待上很多个世纪的东西来说，这种写下来的稳定，可能比一时的热情更有用。
这件事有意思的地方，是它其实回答了三个问题：这些东西在哪里？它们值不值得留下来？我们愿意为“留住”承担多少不方便？岩画在牧区，就意味着放牧、修路、来往的人流都和它共处。一旦决定保护，某些地方可能就不能随便动，某些事就要绕着走。
“千年”这个说法，讲的是时间，也是在讲人。刻下这些图像的人不会想到，许多个世纪之后，会有一群人坐下来，为这些石头写一条规定。下次你在野外看到一块带刻痕的石头，不妨多看一眼——那可能是某个人在很久很久以前，想说的一句话。

title: 研究发现土壤病毒调控深层土壤微生物碳泵
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 科学家把目光投向地下700厘米，发现病毒也许是深层土壤能长期存住碳的一环。
paragraphs: 地球陆地上超过一半的有机碳并不在地表，而在深层土壤里。它们能存很久，一个常被提到的原因是那里的微生物好像都在“休眠”，代谢很慢，碳分解也慢。可后来科学家发现，深层土壤里其实住着一批具备降解几丁质、纤维素和肽聚糖等复杂有机化合物功能的微生物类群，包括CPR细菌和CSP1-3谱系。既然有能把碳拆开的微生物在场，深层土壤的碳为什么还能长期留下来？这个问题一直没解开。

中国科学院生态环境研究中心土壤环境生物学团队联合国内外多家科研机构，在国际期刊《Nature Ecology and Evolution》发表研究论文，揭示了土壤病毒在深层土壤碳持久性中的关键调控机制。研究通过原位土壤剖面调查（0–700 cm）与全球宏基因组数据整合分析，采集并分析了216个宏基因组样本，并结合全球138个土壤剖面、涵盖0–1800 cm深度的1169个扩增子数据和503个宏基因组数据，构建了全球深层土壤病毒数据库（DSVR-DB）。
研究发现，随着土壤深度增加，病毒丰富度显著升高；病毒群落生态策略发生显著性转变，表现为溶原性病毒比例大幅上升。这表明在碳资源极度匮乏的深层环境中，病毒选择“搭便车”策略，通过与宿主细菌协同生存来应对资源限制。

研究发现，深层土壤中的病毒携带大量碳水化合物活性酶（CAZys）辅助代谢基因（AMGs），其中糖苷水解酶（GHs）和内溶素编码基因的丰度随深度增加而显著升高。这些病毒AMGs能够增强宿主细菌对几丁质等复杂聚合物的降解能力，从而缓解深层土壤中的碳限制。研究团队从453个高质量微生物基因组中鉴定出263个携带前病毒的基因组，并发现代表性前病毒通过编码GH23、GH108等降解酶以及热休克蛋白（HSP）、超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）等胁迫响应基因，显著增强了宿主在650–700 cm深层的碳获取能力和环境适应性。
为期16周的微宇宙培养实验结果表明，活性病毒处理组的病毒内溶素活性显著促进了微生物残体碳的积累，进而推动了矿物结合态有机碳（MAOC）的形成。偏最小二乘路径模型（PLS-PM）揭示，病毒裂解对微生物残体碳形成的贡献度（12%）显著高于其他因素。同时，深层土壤中微生物残体与MAOC之间表现为显著正相关，这凸显了病毒介导的微生物碳泵在深层碳封存中的核心作用。

中国科学院生态环境研究中心吴兴杰博士后与河北师范大学韩婉雪博士为论文共同第一作者，肖可青研究员与河北师范大学王凤花副教授为论文共同通讯作者，朱永官研究员参与并提供了关键指导。本研究还与浙江农林大学、中国科学院地球环境研究所、中国科学院城市环境研究所、中国科学院遗传与发育生物学研究所农业资源研究中心、法国里昂大学、德国柏林自由大学等国内外科研机构开展合作。本研究得到中国科学院先导专项和国家自然科学基金等项目资助。

en.title: Soil Viruses Regulate the Deep Soil Microbial Carbon Pump
en.intro: A new study reveals that soil viruses help stabilize carbon in deep soil by partnering with bacteria.
paragraphs: Deep soil stores over half of the terrestrial organic carbon. For a long time, microbiologists believed microbes in deep soil were largely dormant, and their low metabolic activity explained the long-term persistence of soil organic carbon (SOC). However, recent studies found active microbial groups in deep soil capable of degrading complex organic compounds like chitin, cellulose, and peptidoglycan—including CPR bacteria and CSP1–3 lineages. This created a long-standing paradox: how does carbon remain stable if degrading microbes are active?

The study was published in Nature Ecology and Evolution. It was led by the Soil Environmental Biology Team at the Research Center for Eco-Environmental Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in collaboration with domestic and international institutions. The team conducted in situ soil profile surveys across four farmland ecosystems, covering 18 soil layers from 0 to 700 cm depth, and analyzed 216 metagenomic samples. They integrated these with global data: 138 soil profiles (0–1800 cm depth), 1,169 amplicon sequences, and 503 metagenomes—building the Deep Soil Virus Resource Database (DSVR-DB).

The study found virus richness significantly increased with soil depth. Viral community ecological strategies shifted markedly: the proportion of temperate (lysogenic) viruses rose substantially. This suggests viruses adopt a 'hitchhiking' strategy in carbon-poor deep environments—coexisting with bacterial hosts rather than lysing them immediately. Viruses carried abundant auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs), especially carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZys), including glycoside hydrolases (GHs) and endolysin-encoding genes—whose abundances increased significantly with depth.

From 453 high-quality microbial genomes, the team identified 263 prophage-carrying genomes. Representative prophages encoded GH23, GH108, heat shock protein (HSP), and superoxide dismutase (SOD) genes—enhancing host carbon acquisition and environmental adaptability at 650–700 cm depth. In a 16-week microcosm experiment, active virus treatment significantly increased endolysin activity, promoting accumulation of microbial necromass carbon and formation of mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC).

Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) revealed viral lysis contributed 12% to microbial necromass carbon formation—significantly higher than other factors. Critically, microbial necromass showed a significant positive correlation with MAOC—highlighting the central role of virus-mediated microbial carbon pump in deep carbon sequestration.

title: 北美东北部的高山，四十年间悄悄变绿
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 一项用41年卫星影像完成的研究发现，北美东北部88%的高山地带正在变绿，但强风让其中一些山头慢了下来。
paragraphs: 从二十世纪八十年代起，地球整体在变绿。变绿发生在多种生态系统中，包括人口密集区和北极圈以上人迹罕至的区域。高山也在变绿：阿尔卑斯山和落基山脉的植物群落随气候变暖而改变，变得更为葱郁。但在北美东北部，此前尚无系统性、大范围的地理尺度观测。

一项新研究补上了这一空白。该研究发表在《Ecosphere》上，由达特茅斯学院地理学家乔纳森·奇普曼领衔。研究团队使用1984至2024年间近1000幅陆地卫星（Landsat）影像，覆盖新罕布什尔州的白山、纽约州的阿迪朗达克山，以及魁北克加斯佩半岛的山地。他们利用归一化植被指数（NDVI）将影像颜色转化为‘绿度’值并逐年分析。结果显示：这些地区88%的高山区域（约11,352公顷）呈现显著绿化趋势；没有任何站点出现褐化。

奇普曼强调，这是一项遥感研究，并未实地鉴定具体植物种类。但绿度上升表明，植物群落组成很可能正在变化——正从叶片面积小、低矮的高山植物，转向更绿、更灌木状的物种。这种变化可能有多种路径：适应寒冷的高山植物可能逐渐衰退；适应温暖气候的低海拔植物可能向高处迁移并扩大分布；某些高山植物可能因更耐暖而排挤邻近物种；徒步者无意带入的外来种也可能参与其中。此外，二十世纪后期，研究区上风向发电厂排放的大量大气氮沉降，可能曾促进高山植物生长；尽管《清洁空气法》实施后此类排放已大幅减少，其生态影响或仍持续。
瑞士日内瓦大学生态学家阿蒂尔·巴伊尔（Arthur Bayle）未参与本研究。他在邮件中表示，令他惊讶的是，绿化现象在树线以上很高处也尤为显著，说明绿化不仅源于树木向上迁移，还涉及草本、灌木等多类植被本身的转变。他还指出：‘相似的绿化模式，并不意味着相同的生态过程在起作用。’
绿化并非均匀发生。北美东北部以强风著称——例如新罕布什尔州华盛顿山曾记录地面直接观测到的最高风速：每小时231英里（372公里/小时）。奇普曼指出，当地山峰常年受强风影响，使高山区降温，降低绿化敏感性；冬季强风携带冰粒，还会对高山植物造成类似‘喷砂’的物理损伤。因此，在温度主导型高山，变暖常导致更高海拔开始绿化；而在东北部，这一过程更为复杂。巴伊尔认为，强风抑制绿化这一假说‘值得进一步调查’。
这些发现可为保护工作提供依据。绿化速率较慢的区域，环境变化尚未深入，可能仍存留敏感或稀有的高山植物。奇普曼建议：‘例如高度迎风、受绿化影响较小的区域，或许应避免新建步道或基础设施，因为它们未来可能成为高山生物多样性的关键庇护所。’研究团队计划继续追踪绿化缓慢的地点，探究差异成因。奇普曼同时强调：‘这项遥感研究是野外科学的补充，而非替代。’

en.title: Green Peaks: Northeastern Alpine Zones Are Turning Green
en.intro: A new satellite study finds that 88% of alpine areas in northeastern North America have been greening since 1984. Strong winds may explain why some peaks are changing more slowly.
paragraphs: Earth has been getting greener since at least the 1980s. This greening is happening in highly populated areas. It is also happening in largely uninhabited regions above the Arctic Circle. Alpine areas are greening too. Ecosystems in the Alps and the Rocky Mountains have become more verdant. A new study expands scientists’ understanding of this phenomenon in northeastern North America.

Researchers used 41 years of satellite data from 1984 to 2024. They analyzed alpine areas in the White Mountains of New Hampshire. They also analyzed the Adirondacks in New York. And they analyzed the mountains of Quebec’s Gaspé Peninsula. Researchers used nearly 1,000 Landsat images. They used the normalized difference vegetation index. They converted colors into a greenness value. They found that 88% of the alpine area was experiencing significant greening. That is about 11,352 hectares. None of the sites were getting browner.

The study was a remote sensing study. It did not draw conclusions about which plant species were present. Still, the results suggest the composition of plant ecosystems is likely changing. It is shifting from smaller alpine plants with less leaf area to greener, shrubbier species. This can happen in several ways. Cold-adapted alpine plants may slowly die out. Lower-elevation plants adapted to warmer weather may move up in elevation. Some alpine plants may be more resilient. They may outcompete their less resilient neighbors. Invasive species carried by hikers may also contribute. Atmospheric nitrogen from past industrial emissions may have fertilized some peaks.

Arthur Bayle is an ecologist at the Université de Genève. He studies greening in the Alps. He said the study connects satellite observations with deep knowledge of the landscape. He was surprised that greening was pronounced well above the tree line. That suggests greening involved a variety of vegetation. It was not simply upward expansion of trees. The phenomenon was not uniform. One reason may be strong winds. Mount Washington in New Hampshire holds the land record for the highest wind speed ever directly observed. That speed is 231 miles per hour. High winds keep alpine areas cooler. High winds in winter can carry ice particles. That leaves alpine plants essentially sandblasted.

Land managers could use the study’s information. They could identify priority sites for conservation. Places where greening is slower may still host sensitive or rare alpine plants. Highly wind-exposed areas are less subject to greening. Those areas might become important reservoirs of alpine biodiversity in the future. Managers may want to avoid building new infrastructure or trails there. The research team plans to study slower-greening places next. Jonathan Chipman is the study’s lead author. He emphasized that field studies of plant communities are necessary. Satellite studies complement field science. They do not replace it.

title: 美国今年麻疹病例已是去年全年的两倍多，疫情持续扩散
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 一种本可用两针疫苗几乎完全预防的疾病，今年在美国重新扩散，宾夕法尼亚州成为疫情最严重的一州。
paragraphs: 一种本可用两针疫苗几乎完全预防的疾病，今年在美国重新扩散。美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）数据显示，截至10月22日，全美已报告超过4580例麻疹病例，是2025年全年病例数的两倍多。NPR报道指出，这是美国几十年来最严重的麻疹 resurgence（回升）。
疫情最严重的是宾夕法尼亚州。据宾州卫生部上周五通报，今年已在44个县确诊至少1338例麻疹；截至10月21日，新增21例。已有250多人住院，5人死亡。全美范围内，2026年感染麻疹者中96%为‘未接种或接种情况不明’。
在病例最集中的兰开斯特县和米夫林县，受影响最大的是当地阿米什社区——这些社区疫苗接种率偏低。5名死者中，3人居住在兰开斯特县。上周四，宾州卫生部长德布拉·博根博士与米夫林县医护人员举行圆桌会，评估当地防控需求。她说：‘我们的州级指标和数据只讲了这次疫情的一部分故事，而倾听一线照护者讲述受疫情影响社区的真实情况，对完善公共卫生响应至关重要。’
卫生官员表示，接种疫苗是预防麻疹最有效的方式之一。麻疹、腮腺炎、风疹三联疫苗（MMR）接种两剂对麻疹的保护效力近97%，单剂约93%。宾州卫生部门称，10月前三周全州共接种超3.9万剂麻疹疫苗，高于平常一个月约2.5万剂的平均接种量。
其他州也在应对疫情。纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔本月宣布该州进入灾难紧急状态；截至10月20日，纽约州已确诊超160例麻疹。犹他州今年确诊超700例，但据该州卫生与人类服务部称，最近三周无新发诊断。南卡罗来纳州2026年至少报告997例，疫情已于4月结束。

title: 渣土和淤泥，怎样变成建筑用的石头
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 城市挖出的渣土和淤泥，除了填埋和焚烧，还能在本地变成建筑用的石头。
paragraphs: 10月24日，2026世界青年科学家峰会在浙江温州园博园拉开帷幕。在峰会展示交流活动现场，一块块由工程渣土、河道淤泥转化而来的生态石材整齐陈列，观感和质地与天然石料别无二致。从会场走向园博园，这种‘变废为宝’的体验愈发真切：脚下的铺地石、路边的路沿石、错落的假山与桥梁，大多由园区自身产出的建筑渣土就地加工再造而成。就地消纳、就地生产、就地应用，一条‘点废成金’的循环链条在此形成完整闭环。

固体废弃物价值化、资源化利用，是当前我国推进绿色低碳转型的重要命题。城市建设和工业生产每天产生大量固废，如煤矸石、粉煤灰、工业尾矿渣、农作物秸秆等，种类繁多、体量庞大。长期以来，对这些大宗固废，最主要的处置方式是填埋和焚烧。填埋虽然简单，却持续占用土地，堆存产生的渗滤液与扬尘还可能污染土壤和地下水；焚烧则依赖高温，能耗高、碳排放可观。并且，无论填埋还是焚烧，都绕不开远距离运输，途中产生的废气、废水与扬尘，又给城市添上一重负担。今年初，国务院颁布《固体废物综合治理行动计划》，进一步把大宗固废物综合利用提上重要日程，治理思路也从‘能处置、少污染’转向‘减量化、资源化’并重。
浙江星创环保集团总裁邵璋介绍这项全国首创的‘淤泥制石’核心技术，做的正是让渣土‘重回’岩石状态。研发团队历时五年攻关，从血浆分离技术中获得启发，通过纳米级改性改变淤泥的亲水性，实现固液高效分离，并模拟自然界岩石风化的逆过程，使废弃渣土在低温高压下重新结晶。整套生产工艺摒弃了传统建材的高温烧制流程，依托千吨级真空压制设备完成固废物料的标准化处理。

生态石产品售价较天然石材降低30%左右，制品中固废含量可达40%以上，高于行业平均水平。在温州园博园项目中，生态石应用总量超过1万立方米，相较外购天然石材节约建设成本600余万元。目前，该成套技术已形成规模化应用能力，可对建筑渣土、盾构泥、河道淤泥、市政污泥、油泥尾渣、焚烧飞灰、煤矸石等18大类固废进行资源化处置，成功转化出无机生态石、护坡石、固化土、仿木板材、生物质燃料等八大类高附加值绿色产品，覆盖市政建设、园林景观、基础建材等多个应用领域。
‘渣土制石’，为地球少开一座山，让青山常在。这种‘本地产生、本地处理、本地利用’的闭环已从温州走向全国，在杭州、上海、深圳、重庆等70余座城市落地生根。面向未来，星创环保规划在全国100座城市落地500条生产线，朝着百亿级循环产业集群目标稳步迈进；同时联动泰国、越南、印度尼西亚、哈萨克斯坦等国家，对外输出中国固废资源化成套解决方案。

title: 不用贵金属，分子筛也能给分子加上碳和氧
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 中国科学家用分子筛直接催化烯烃羰基化，绕开了铑、铱等贵金属，新反应连续稳定运行750小时。
paragraphs: 给一个分子同时装上一个碳和一个氧，化学上叫“羰基化”。这道“加法题”听起来轻巧，却能创造出诸多高附加值的化学品。从医药中间体到可降解塑料单体、从溶剂到香料，羰基化反应撑起了现代化学工业的一大片天。百余年来，工业上主流的方法是依赖铑、铱等贵金属配合物催化，还需卤素助剂参与，体系复杂、配体昂贵、催化剂与产物难分离。
有没有可能换一条路，不用金属也能把碳和氧“装”上去？10月21日，《自然》发表了中国科学院大连化学物理研究所（以下简称大连化物所）研究员刘中民团队的研究，给出了一个肯定的答案：他们通过分子筛空间限域调控的催化策略，实现了水参与的分子筛直接催化的乙烯羰基化到丙酸和丙烯羰基化到异丁酸两个反应。
团队为什么盯上烯烃？我国煤基甲醇制烯烃产业布局迅速，烯烃来源丰富、成本可控。从烯烃切入羰基化，有利于布局煤基高附加值含氧化合物的生产路线，能够把丰富的烯烃变成丙酸、异丁酸这些精细化学品。但烯烃在分子筛的酸性位上容易聚合，副反应会迅速让催化剂失活，因此既要让羰基化容易发生，又要抑制副反应。

分子筛是一类具有规整孔道结构的无机多孔晶体材料，具有精准的孔道筛选能力，在石油炼制、气体分离和化工生产中发挥着不可替代的作用。2017年，刘中民团队就成功利用分子筛催化的二甲醚羰基化反应，实现无水乙醇的大规模工业化生产，验证了分子筛在羰基化上的巨大潜力。这一次，他们提出利用分子筛的限域效应：孔道的空间约束如同一双“巧手”，将反应物摆放在合适的位置，让一氧化碳能够精准插入，而不给聚合反应留出空间。他们尝试了大量可能的分子筛结构，最终发现镁碱沸石（FER）在当前探索的体系中最为适宜。
团队在FER上实现了乙烯与一氧化碳、水反应生成丙酸，丙烯与一氧化碳、水反应生成异丁酸。小试实验确认了两个反应在高压条件下可连续运行750小时，丙酸选择性约80%，异丁酸选择性高达95%。该反应属于首次报道，领域内没有类似的工作可供参照。从工业化角度看，性能仍有待进一步提升和优化，但750小时的稳定性已经展现出很好的应用潜力。2025年6月，团队首次将成果投稿至《自然》，16个月后被正式接收。
这项工作的意义远不止于两个新反应。丙酸和异丁酸都是重要精细化学品，也都是甲基丙烯酸甲酯的潜在前驱体，而甲基丙烯酸甲酯是生产有机玻璃的大宗单体。如果技术后续放大落地，可能带来丙酸和异丁酸的新生产工艺，下游衍生物具备更高价值。相较于传统液体酸催化，分子筛非均相体系可实现连续、高效生产，而且不用处理含酸废水，环保优势明显。
团队还在努力回答一个更大的问题——能否建立通用框架，反过来预测并设计更多分子筛催化的羰基化新过程。烯烃羰基化的成功，为搭建该通用框架补上了关键拼图。一旦这套通用框架成功建立，分子筛催化羰基化反应就不再依赖经验试错，而是走向理性设计与精准预测，为含氧化合物的高效、绿色制备打开更广阔的空间。

title: 重要里程碑！中国散裂中子源束流功率突破200kW
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 据中新网教育报道，中国散裂中子源束流功率突破200kW，被称作一个重要里程碑。
paragraphs: 据中新网教育报道，中国散裂中子源束流功率突破200kW，被称作一个重要里程碑。
中国散裂中子源是一种大科学装置。它通过将质子加速后轰击靶材，使原子核发生散裂，从而产生中子。中子不带电，能穿透多种材料，与原子核相互作用后改变运动方向和能量；科学家通过探测这些中子的飞行路径和能量分布，反推材料内部原子结构。
束流功率指单位时间内质子束输送给靶材的能量，单位为kW。功率越高，产生的中子通量通常越大，有助于缩短实验时间、提升测量精度和信噪比。因此，束流功率是衡量散裂中子源性能的核心指标之一。
提高束流功率需同步提升加速器稳定性、靶站耐辐照能力、束流控制精度及辐射防护水平，涉及多系统协同优化，技术难度大、周期长。此次突破200kW，标志着装置性能实现重要跃升。
该装置能力提升后，将支撑更多前沿科学研究，包括新型能源材料、高温超导机制、生物大分子结构解析等领域。

title: 一棵菊花，怎样开出一千朵花
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 在美国宾夕法尼亚州的长木花园，上千朵菊花其实长在同一棵植物上；园艺师花了大约十八个月，才把它一点点变成这个样子。
paragraphs: 在美国宾夕法尼亚州的长木花园，游客常常在一株植物前停下脚步，猜它到底是什么。远远看过去，它是一个巨大的花团：上百——甚至上千——朵菊花，每一朵都待在该在的位置上，从边缘向顶部一圈一圈升起来，创造一种丰盛到近乎奢侈的印象。很多人第一反应是：这一定是用许多盆菊花拼起来的。但答案出人意料：这一整团花，全都长在同一棵菊花上（Chrysanthemum x morifolium）。花团底下，几百根枝条汇聚到同一根茎、同一套根系统。看上去成千上万，其实只有一棵。

要把一棵菊花变成这样，大约需要十八个月。长木花园每年六月开始动手，起点是十根扦插的枝条。秋天夜里越来越长，园艺师就用人工灯光把长夜打断，让植株保持营养生长状态，不急着开花。接着是掐尖：掐掉一根枝条的顶端，它就分成两根；再掐，两根变四根，就这样一路分下去，直到超过一千根枝条。到了十一月，他们从十棵里挑出两棵最强壮的，同时养着，互为备份。花盆和支架跟着植株一起变大，枝条被绑在定制的框架上，光照、水分、养分、温度和生长都要仔细平衡。直到展览前不久，才从这两棵里定下最终上场的那一棵。
枝条够多了，重点就转到花上。每根枝条会长出好几个花蕾，园艺师只留下最顶端的那一个，把旁边的侧蕾全部摘掉，这一步叫摘蕾（disbudding）。养分集中到一朵花上，花才会开得又大又整齐。整个培养过程，绑结可能用掉四千多个。有时候为了让枝条弯到合适的位置又不至于折断，他们会故意让枝条暂时萎蔫一点，软下来再定型。
展览前大约一个月，进入最后阶段。每一朵花都要装上一个用金属丝做的托架，日语里叫 rindai，用来托住花的重量，也用来精确调整每朵花的朝向。一千多个 rindai，一个一个装上去，光这一项就要花掉大约十天。而所有这些反复的调整，最后看起来必须毫不费力。

这种做法在日本有个名字，叫 ōzukuri， commonly translated as “large cultivation”。菊花原产中国，栽培技术几百年前传到日本，日本园艺师发展出一整套方法，把植株训练成特定的正式形状。1884 年，东京的新宿御苑第一次做出这种形式：一棵植物，几百朵花，排成一个比例讲究的宽大花团，后来的千朵菊都以它为样板。这个年份也有讲究：十九世纪末的日本正处于快速变革期，明治政府在推动现代化的同时，也在寻找能向世界展示本国文化的象征形式；菊花因与皇室渊源深厚，因而格外突出。
和石头刻成的雕像不同，千朵菊一直在生长，也一直在衰败。它的活体组织持续生长、蒸腾、响应环境并老化。园艺师不是把一张完成的图样按在一棵植物上；他是在和一个活的形状反复商量：未来可以影响，却没法完全控制。所以每一次掐尖，都是对还没长出来的部分下注；每一次剪掉一根枝条、一个花蕾，都是放弃一种可能，让另一种可能长大。秋天你看到的那棵菊花，既由培育出来的部分组成，也由一路上被舍掉的部分组成。

en.title: One Plant, a Thousand Blooms
en.intro: A garden in Pennsylvania grows more than a thousand chrysanthemum flowers on a single plant. This uses a centuries-old Japanese tradition.
paragraphs: From a distance, the plant appears to be an immense floral dome. It is composed of hundreds—if not a thousand—of carefully matched chrysanthemums. Each flower occupies its own place in a near-perfect pattern. Visitors often wonder if multitudes of plants have been assembled. Then comes the revelation: every blossom belongs to a single chrysanthemum.

Beneath the dome, hundreds of branches converge toward a single stem and root system. What appears to be a multitude is actually one plant. Its scientific name is Chrysanthemum x morifolium. It is cultivated over approximately eighteen months. It is guided through thousands of individual decisions. At Longwood, the annual creation begins with ten vegetative cuttings. These are started each June. Artificial light interrupts the long autumn nights. This keeps the chrysanthemums vegetative. Horticulturists pinch the growing tips. This encourages one stem to divide into two, then four, until reaching over one thousand stems. By November, the two strongest plants are selected. They are carried forward in parallel.

Both plants are continually trained and tied to custom-made frames. The frames support the increasing weight of the stems. They also help establish the balance and form of the eventual dome. Shoots are selected or removed. Light, water, nutrition, temperature, and growth are carefully balanced. As more than one thousand stems begin to set buds, the focus shifts. It shifts from increasing their number to perfecting the flowers they will bear. Through disbudding, competing lateral buds are removed from each stem. This leaves a single terminal bud to develop. This concentrates the plant’s resources. It helps produce large, uniform blooms.

Once the final display plant is selected, about a month before exhibition, the work enters its last stage. Each developing flower is fitted with an individual wire support. This support is called a rindai. The rindai bears the weight of the bloom. It allows horticulturists to orient the flower precisely within the dome. More than one thousand rindai may be individually attached. This process alone can take about ten days. The work requires constant adjustment. Yet the completed form must look effortless.

The Japanese name for the Thousand Bloom form is ōzukuri. It is commonly translated as 'large cultivation.' The chrysanthemum originated in China. Its cultivation traveled to Japan centuries ago. Japanese growers developed new systems for training the plant. They trained it into distinctive formal shapes. The ōzukuri form was first created at Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden in Tokyo in 1884. It established a model for the Thousand Bloom Chrysanthemum. That model has hundreds of flowers. They grow from a single plant. They are arranged into a broad and carefully proportioned dome. In Japan, chrysanthemums came to signify autumn, renewal, refined taste, and imperial authority.

For approximately eighteen months, time accumulates in the plant. Then, for only a few weeks each fall, time becomes visible. This happens when the Thousand Bloom is displayed. Unlike sculptures carved from stone, the Thousand Bloom is always becoming—or ceasing to be. Its living tissue continues to grow. It transpires. It responds. It ages. The horticulturist who trains it is not imposing a finished image. They are negotiating with a living form. The future of that form can be influenced. But it can never be completely controlled. Every pinch is performed in expectation of growth that has not yet occurred. Every selected branch commits the horticulturist to a future arrangement. Every removed shoot or bud sacrifices one possibility. Another possibility may flourish. The plant visitors see in the autumn is composed of what was cultivated. It is also composed of what was deliberately relinquished.

title: 哈尔滨头骨被藏枯井后，为何有了龙人和丹尼索瓦人两个名字
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 1933年被工人藏进枯井的哈尔滨头骨，如今有了两个名字：龙人（Homo longi），和丹尼索瓦人。
paragraphs: 2018年9月，《中国日报》的一篇报道摆到了研究人类起源的学者桌上。照片里是一具保存得异常完好的头骨化石，眉骨粗壮得惊人。当时的图注猜测它属于海德堡人（Homo heidelbergensis），这个猜测后来被证明是错的。报道讲述了它被发现的故事：1933年，日军占领哈尔滨，命令一队本地工人在松花江上修铁路桥。工人们在河床沉积物里挖出了这具头骨，其中一人为了不让日本人拿走，把它吊进一口废弃的水井里藏了起来。他因为给敌人干活而感到羞耻，很多年没有作声。直到大约八十年后，临终前他才把这件事告诉儿子和孙子，头骨因此被找回，后来捐给了北京附近的河北地质大学。这个故事很难核实，甚至有过这具化石是赝品的传言。但2018年底，作者受邀和中国研究者一起研究它，亲眼确认了它是真的。

要理解它的意义，得先放下一个旧印象：人类演化不是从原始形态一步步走向现代人的单线阶梯。我们和黑猩猩的祖先大约七百万年前分开，之后约五百万年，人类祖先一直在非洲演化，大约两百万年前才开始向亚洲和欧洲扩散。自然界在几百万年里反复试验‘怎样才算成为人’，结果是出现了一大群不同的人种，有时同时存在，甚至住在同一片地区。我们是这些试验里唯一的幸存者。就在最近三十万年里，人种数量也令人吃惊。海德堡人三十万年前还生活在欧洲；更古老的直立人（Homo erectus）脑子更小、头顶扁平，至少十万年前还留在印度尼西亚的部分地区；尼安德特人（Homo neanderthalensis）至少在四十万年前到四万年前生活在欧亚西部；我们智人（Homo sapiens）至少三十万年前出现在非洲，最近五万年内走向全球。此外还有三种体型很小的人——纳莱迪人（Homo naledi）、弗洛勒斯人（Homo floresiensis）和吕宋人（Homo luzonensis）——分别生活在南非、印尼的弗洛勒斯岛和菲律宾的吕宋岛，看起来都像是更古老阶段的遗存。

哈尔滨这具头骨给这份名单又添了一个物种。中国同事给作者寄来全尺寸的3D打印件时，他不敢相信自己的眼睛。他见过几百具人类头骨化石，这是最大的一具。分析显示，它和智人、尼安德特人、海德堡人、直立人都明显不同：脑容量很大，眉脊巨大；脑颅又大又低，但表面比较平滑，没有直立人和海德堡人头上那些骨脊；面部很大却相当现代，颧骨细致、朝前，鼻子很宽，眼窝很大。2021年，中国同事把它命名为龙人（Homo longi），名字来自黑龙江（Heilongjiang River）。这个物种至少在三十万年前到大约四万五千年前生活在东亚。
头骨还解开了别的谜。关键是它唯一保留下来的那颗牙：一颗非常大的第二臼齿，后面没有第三臼齿的齿槽。换句话说，龙人没有智齿。这个牙齿特征把中国境内另外一些不完整的化石联系了起来，它们也是大臼齿、没有智齿。这说明它们同样属于龙人，推翻了此前两种猜测：它们可能属于海德堡人的亚洲分支，或者属于直立人和现代亚洲人之间的过渡类型。

它还解释了丹尼索瓦人的身份。丹尼索瓦人得名于阿尔泰山脉俄罗斯一侧的丹尼索瓦洞。考古学家在那里挖了几十年，找到成千上万件动物骨骼和石器，人类骨骼却只有碎片和几颗大臼齿。2010年，其中一块小指骨碎片产出了质量堪比现代骨骼的古DNA，而它已有大约六万年；这说明西伯利亚南部那个寒冷干燥的洞穴保存遗骸的能力多么惊人。靠着其他化石甚至洞穴沉积物里的DNA，我们知道丹尼索瓦人断断续续住在洞里，从二十多万年前一直到大约四万五千年前，之后智人接管。同样在2010年，科学家从欧洲化石里重建出高质量的尼安德特人基因组，而丹尼索瓦人的基因组和尼安德特人、和现代人都相当不同。十年后，分析表明丹尼索瓦洞里那些大臼齿也属于和龙人头骨同一个物种。更近一些，研究者从哈尔滨头骨中提取DNA和化石蛋白，确认了它和丹尼索瓦洞、以及中国其他化石的联系：青藏高原高处洞穴里的下颌骨、台湾渔民从海里捞上来的骨头，还有中国西南一个洞穴里最近描述的遗存。
所以这具头骨，是古人类学家追踪了很久的那个物种目前最完整的标本。它现在有两个名字：丹尼索瓦人，和更正式的龙人（Homo longi）。一具在废井里躺了八十年的头骨，最终让人看到：成为人从来不是一条独木桥，而是一条分叉很多的河，我们只是其中侥幸流到今天的那一支。

en.title: The Dragon Man Skull and Our Human Story
en.intro: A remarkably complete skull from China is helping scientists piece together a lost chapter of human evolution.
paragraphs: In September 2018, a China Daily story about a fossil skull reached the desk of a scientist who studies human origins. The skull had been found in Harbin, in north-eastern China, in 1933. Japanese forces were occupying the city and ordered local workers to help build a railway bridge across the Songhua River. The workers uncovered the skull in river deposits. One of them hid it from the Japanese by lowering it down a disused well. Feeling ashamed of having worked for the enemy, he kept quiet about the find for many years. Finally, some 80 years later, he told his son and grandson as he lay dying. That led to the almost intact skull being recovered and later donated to Hebei Geo University near Beijing.

That origin story is difficult to verify, and there were rumours that the fossil was actually a fake. The scientist was invited to join Chinese researchers in studying this astonishing relic at the end of 2018. He confirmed first hand that it was real. It was one of the most complete human fossils ever found. He jumped at this wonderful opportunity to help put it in its proper place in human evolution.

Human evolution was not a simple straight line from primitive forms to modern humans. Hominins split from the ancestors of chimpanzees about 7 million years ago. For the next 5 million years or so, hominins continued their evolution in Africa. About 2 million years ago, they began to disperse across Asia and Europe. Nature conducted multiple experiments over millions of years in how to become human. Different kinds of humans sometimes lived at the same time and even in the same regions. We are the sole survivors of all those experiments.

The Harbin skull was the biggest fossil human skull the scientist had ever seen. Analyses showed it was clearly different from fossils of Homo sapiens, Homo neanderthalensis, Homo heidelbergensis and Homo erectus. It had a very large brain size, a massive brow-ridge, and a large, low but rather smooth braincase. It also had a big but modern-looking face with delicate forward-facing cheekbones, a very wide nose, and large eye sockets. In 2021, Chinese colleagues named the new species Homo longi, named after the Black Dragon River (Heilongjiang). Ever since, the skull has been known as Dragon Man. This species appears to have lived in eastern Asia from at least 300,000 until about 45,000 years ago.

The skull’s single preserved tooth was a very large second molar, with no sign of a socket behind it for a third molar. In other words, Dragon Man did not have wisdom teeth. These dental features provided a link with other less complete fossils from China that also had large molars but no wisdom teeth. This and other resemblances indicated that those fossils were also Homo longi. It also shed light on the mysterious Denisovans, named after Denisova Cave in the Russian part of the Altai Mountains. A finger bone from the cave yielded ancient DNA matching the quality of modern bones — despite being about 60,000 years old. The Denisovans occupied the cave intermittently from more than 200,000 until about 45,000 years ago. Later analyses of the Harbin skull for DNA and fossil proteins confirmed both the connection to Denisova Cave and various other fossils found in China. The skull is now known by both names: Denisovan and the more formal Homo longi.

title: 蚊子为什么偏爱某些人，线索可能在皮肤气味和细菌里
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 一项新研究发现，不同种类的蚊子偏爱不同的人，原因或许藏在皮肤气味和皮肤上的细菌里。
paragraphs: 夏天里常能看到这样的场面：同一群人待在一起，有人被蚊子咬得满腿是包，有人却几乎没事。一项新研究发现，这或许和每个人皮肤上的化学物质以及住在皮肤上的微生物有关。而且，不同种类的蚊子，口味还不一样。
蚊子寻找吸血对象，靠的是视觉、气味线索，还有人体的热量。可一个人的气味里，能包含超过一千种化学物质，想弄清哪一种最影响蚊子的选择并不容易。为了找出答案，位于迈阿密的佛罗里达国际大学的研究者马修·德詹纳罗和同事招募了一百一十九位志愿者，让三种蚊子分别‘闻’他们的气味。

实验用的装置能让笼子里的蚊子闻到人的气味，却咬不到人。埃及伊蚊（_Aedes aegypti_）和白纹伊蚊（_Aedes albopictus_）在白天进食，志愿者可以白天到实验室，把手臂伸进装置。致倦库蚊（_Culex quinquefasciatus_）只在夜里出来觅食，研究者就让志愿者先戴上尼龙袖套几个小时，收集他们的气味，到了晚上再把袖套放进装置。研究者数一数有多少蚊子凑过来，以此判断它们对每个人气味的兴趣有多大。研究结果于8月21日发表在期刊《iScience》上。
三种蚊子挑中的人并不相同。有的人能同时吸引不止一种蚊子，但没有哪一位志愿者是三种蚊子共同的最爱。埃及伊蚊和致倦库蚊更喜欢皮肤气味较淡的人；白纹伊蚊则被13种闻起来像植物的化学物质吸引。这种差别说明，每种蚊子可能各自演化出了找吸血对象的办法。
不过，人体气味非常复杂。研究蚊子气味的玛丽亚·埃莱娜·德奥巴尔迪亚说，要把其中的化学物质一种一种检测出来很难，所以可能还有别的有吸引力的化合物没被这项研究找到。另一位研究者艾丽西亚·舒韦林则提醒，每种蚊子吸食哪些动物、又在什么时间觅食，都可能影响它们的选择。

研究团队还把目光转向皮肤上的细菌。我们气味里的很多化学物质，正是微生物制造出来的。他们擦拭志愿者的皮肤取样，发现某些细菌对三种蚊子都有吸引力。接下来，他们想弄清楚这些细菌怎样造出影响蚊子选择的气味，这或许能带来新的驱蚊办法：比如让人的气味不那么招蚊子，或者用最有吸引力的化学物质做诱饵，把蚊子引进陷阱。‘我们都在努力弄清楚怎样阻止人们生病，’研究主要作者凯莉·马雷罗说，‘弄清蚊子为什么咬人，是实现这个目标的最佳途径。’

title: 我国科学家破解丹尼索瓦人辨识难题
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 中国科学院古脊椎动物与古人类研究所科研人员结合古蛋白质组学与化石形态对比，确认河北阳原许家窑人属于丹尼索瓦人，并首次建立起丹尼索瓦人的形态识别标准。
paragraphs: 有一支古人类，科学家认识他们已经快十六年了，却一直不知道他们究竟长什么样。现在，这个问题第一次有了答案。记者从中国科学院古脊椎动物与古人类研究所获悉，该所科研人员确认，河北阳原的许家窑人，就是丹尼索瓦人。

丹尼索瓦人是一支已经灭绝的古老人类支系。2010年，科学家依靠西伯利亚丹尼索瓦洞化石的DNA证据发现了这一人群。后续分子证据显示，丹尼索瓦人曾广泛分布在亚洲多地，生存时间大约在距今30万年至4.5万年前。长久以来，一个难题困扰学界：丹尼索瓦人只能靠分子信号识别，我们不知道丹尼索瓦人到底长什么样，没有一套像尼安德特人、现代人那样清晰的外形判定标准，东亚大量同时期古人类化石到底是不是丹尼索瓦人，一直没有明确答案。
位于河北阳原的许家窑遗址，是东亚中更新世晚期最重要的古人类遗址之一，距今19.9万到13.8万年。这里出土了20件古人类化石，至少代表16个不同个体，还伴生大量石球等石制品与动物化石，地层清楚、材料丰富，是解开谜题的理想材料。由于年代久远，化石里的古DNA已经很难保存，于是中国科学院古脊椎动物与古人类研究所付巧妹、邢松等科研人员联合南京师范大学、北京大学等单位，转向古蛋白质组学开展攻关研究。
科研团队从许家窑人头骨、下颌骨化石微量骨粉中提取了古蛋白，找到丹尼索瓦人独有的蛋白变异位点，系统发育分析证实，许家窑人就是丹尼索瓦人。以此为锚点，团队对比哈尔滨人、夏河人等已确认的丹尼索瓦人化石，梳理出颅骨、下颌骨、牙齿上一套独有的形态组合特征，区分于直立人、尼安德特人和现代人。
研究团队进一步比对了金牛山、大荔、华龙洞等多处东亚古人类化石发现，这些中更新世晚期古人类，形态特征和许家窑丹尼索瓦人高度契合，大概率同属这一支古人类。这意味着丹尼索瓦人的活动范围几乎覆盖整个东亚大陆，适应能力远超此前认知。相关研究成果10月21日在国际学术期刊《自然》发表。
这项研究首次建立起丹尼索瓦人的形态识别标准，为厘清东亚中更新世人类演化格局补上关键一环。

title: 伦敦牛津街将对车辆关闭，希望重新变成人们愿意停留的街道
author: 轻听编辑部
intro: 欧洲最繁忙的购物街即将对车辆关门，伦敦希望这条几乎没人说喜欢的街道，能重新变成人们愿意停留的地方。
paragraphs: 伦敦人几乎没人愿意承认自己喜欢牛津街。可这条街每天有超过五十万人经过，相当于把整个爱丁堡的人口搬上来一次。它是欧洲最繁忙的购物街，贡献伦敦经济产出的百分之五；每年两千两百万到伦敦的外国游客，多数大概都在某个时刻踩上过它。就是这样一条街，下周一，10月26日，要对车辆关门了。

禁行范围是牛津街1.2英里中的一半——0.6英里，从牛津 Circus 交叉口附近一直向西，到塞尔福里奇百货。汽车、货车、面包车、出租车、公交、自行车、电动自行车、滑板车一律禁止进入，只留行人和紧急车辆。这是至少自2003年特拉法加广场从一个大环岛改造成公共空间以来，伦敦市中心街景最显著的变化。伦敦市长萨迪克·汗在2026年2月宣布了这个决定。三年前他出版回忆录《呼吸》，书中将自己从小患哮喘归因于在伦敦吸入受污染的空气。

牛津街确实需要一次大修。它窄，两边楼高，形成一个‘城市峡谷’，把公交和出租车排出的柴油废气闷在里头。2014年，这里的二氧化氮浓度被测得是全球最高。同一年，犯罪严重到阿联酋政府警告本国公民避开这个区域。疫情和网购又给了它一击：店铺空置率从2019年的4.5%，涨到2023年初的16.9%。填补空铺的，是一些来历不明的美国糖果店和空荡荡的纪念品店，据称靠逃税维持。汗在2024年承认，这是一种‘管理式衰退’。

接下改造设计的是伦敦一家叫East的建筑事务所。他们不做房子，做房子外面的世界：标识、长椅、路缘、铺装、灯光、花箱、树，还有公共艺术。近三十年，他们做了近三十个高街改造项目。负责人朱利安·刘易斯和阿尔奇·巴什福德去年中标后，第一件事是翻档案。他们找到一个起点：1932年，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在《好管家》杂志上写过一篇关于牛津街的文章。伍尔夫把它比作‘一条巨大的滚动丝带’，‘一条河的卵石河床’，被‘明亮的溪流’冲刷。她嫌它俗艳，但也觉得它闪耀、刺激、让人招架不住，而这一切来自街上杂乱人群的不停流动。设计团队把这个河流的意象，落成了很具体的决定：光怎么落在表面上，长椅和柱子怎么微微反光。他们打算先摆一些盆栽的小树，加上新的座椅。从下周到2027年春天是测试期，看看人们怎么用这些树：会不会变成约见面的地方，歇脚的地方，认路的地标。
人行化是一件事，让牛津街变成人们真想待着的地方是另一件事。刘易斯对分隔人行区的路桩很有意见，他把路桩当人来说。他说，路桩通常是可怕的东西，太常显得‘抱歉’。一条歪掉的、塑料感的反光条，传递的信息是‘对不起，我其实不想在这儿，但我得让你知道附近有车’。他说，路桩应该说：‘我很高兴在这儿，因为我在做一份工作。’

source.originalTitle: Everyone hates Oxford Street. Will pedestrianisation save it?

en.title: Oxford Street Goes Car-Free
en.intro: A Guardian Long Read looks at London's plan to close Europe's busiest shopping street to traffic.
paragraphs: Oxford Street is the busiest shopping street in Europe. On Monday, 26 October, half of its 1.2-mile stretch will be closed to traffic. Cars, lorries, vans, taxis, buses, bicycles, e-bikes, and scooters will be banned. Only pedestrians and emergency vehicles will be allowed in. The mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, announced the pedestrianisation plan in February. To the surprise of many Londoners, it is actually happening.

This change marks the most remarkable transformation to central London's streetscape since at least 2003, when Trafalgar Square was turned into one of London's most recognisable public spaces. It will form the most visible part of the mayor’s legacy. Khan attributes his asthma to growing up inhaling London’s polluted air. For him, pedestrianising Oxford Street is the culmination of a mission to create a greener city oriented around public health, walking and cycling. In 2014, Oxford Street was found to have the highest concentration of nitrogen dioxide pollution in the world. Its narrow streetway and tall buildings trap diesel fumes from buses and taxis.

Pedestrianisation is one thing; making Oxford Street somewhere anyone actually wants to spend time is another. Its primary associations are crowds, stress, dirt, noise, tacky consumer capitalism, and crime. A police officer said pedestrianisation would be both good for the street and make her job harder. Oxford Street receives more than 500,000 visitors every day — equivalent to the population of Edinburgh. It generates 5% of the capital’s economic output. And yet, nobody loves Oxford Street. During the course of writing this article, the author did not meet anyone who would even admit to liking it.

Vacancy levels on Oxford Street soared from 4.5% in 2019 to 16.9% by early 2023. Covid and internet shopping hit it hard. Raids have hauled in counterfeit goods and illegal vapes. US candy stores and empty souvenir shops have appeared. In 2024, Khan conceded the street was in 'managed decline'. His gamble is that pedestrianisation will reverse that decline and flood the street with life again.

The design team East is leading the redesign. They studied a 1932 article by Virginia Woolf in Good Housekeeping. She described Oxford Street as a 'great rolling ribbon … the pebbly bed of a river … washed by a bright stream'. The pedestrianised zone will run from close to the Oxford Circus crossing to Selfridges — 0.6 miles. The test phase lasts until spring 2027. The plan includes young trees in pots and new places to sit. The team will learn how people respond: will the trees become meeting points, rest stops, or landmarks for wayfinding? Bollards will mark the edges. One architect said bollards should look 'happy to be here, because I’m doing a job.'
The real test begins after the traffic disappears. Can Oxford Street become a place where people want to linger?
